title: Compose design-system primitives for interactive controls in app code

facts.note: Component source (.tsx/.jsx) and HTML authored in string/template/tagged-template literals in .ts/.mts; plain .html is out of scope.

Only app code outside the design root; tests and vendored/build dirs never scanned. The source names vendored/build directories without concrete globs; the verifier's own vendored/build exclusion list applies.
Evaluated at repository scope: a design root must exist in the repository; without one the rule is not judged (self-scoping).

values: raw <button|<input|<select|<textarea added or present in app code
facts.note: Requires the bun_design_system_detector (JSX scan plus literal-only scan of .ts/.mts) to report raw_control findings.

fires: A .tsx/.jsx component outside the design root renders a raw <button> while the repo has a design/ directory with primitives.
A .ts/.mts server-rendered (htmx/Bun) handler returns a template literal containing `<input ` outside the design root.
A tagged-template literal in a .mts file contains `<select>` or `<textarea/` in app code, in any phase (including REFACTOR or review of existing code).
doesNotFire: The repository has no design, design_system, or design-system directory.
A primitive under the design root renders a raw <button>.
A *.test.* or *.spec.* file, or a vendored/build directory, contains raw controls.
A .ts file has `a <input` in code position (comparison), an angle-bracket type assertion, a comment, or a regex literal mentioning <button.

given: App code outside a design root (design/design_system/design-system): .tsx/.jsx, or .ts/.mts HTML in string/template/tagged-template literals (htmx/Bun shape).
then: Render it through a design-system primitive, never a raw lowercase <button>, <input>, <select>, or <textarea>.
prefer: Use the existing primitive; pass required htmx/DOM attributes through it.
During GREEN: reuse the primitive that already represents the control.
During GREEN: extend only the smallest prop/attribute surface the current interaction requires.
During GREEN: create a new primitive only if none represents the control correctly.
avoid: Raw interactive markup bypassing the primitive just to pass the acceptance.
Generic primitive props the current behavior does not need.
unless: No design root in the repo (nothing to connect to yet; not judged).
why: Controls hold focus, disabled, error and loading states; each raw control re-implements them and diverges. Primitives keep controls themed, accessible, consistent.
evidence: The bun_design_system_detector reports no raw_control findings in .tsx/.jsx or .ts/.mts literal HTML outside the design root.
Prove: the rendered interactive control comes through the design-system primitive.
verifier_detail: design_root: a directory named `design`, `design_system`, or `design-system`. The first directory beneath it names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`. A repository with no design root is not judged (self-scoping): there is no system to connect to yet.

raw_control: a lowercase `<button`, `<input`, `<select`, or `<textarea` element written in app code — in JSX, or in the body of a string/template/tagged-template literal in a `.ts`/`.mts` file — followed by whitespace, `>`, or `/`.
Scope summary: flags raw interactive platform elements in component source (.tsx/.jsx) and in `.ts`/`.mts` literal HTML outside the design root.

Only literal text is judged in `.ts`/`.mts` files: code position (comparisons, angle-bracket type assertions), comments, and regex literals are never treated as markup, and a control spanning a `${…}` interpolation is read on its literal chunks alone.
Never scanned: test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`), vendored/build directories, the design system's own primitives (they render the raw elements), plain `.html` templates.
Disposition strict, severity 2: every finding fails.
audit: Source fix_hint headings: 'Canonical path:' (prefer[0]), 'During GREEN:' (prefer[1..3]), 'Do not broaden:' (avoid[0..2]), 'Prove:' (evidence[1..2]).

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire example situations and the observability classification of facts.
additions.justification: Required by the output schema; derived directly from source scope and exceptions, no new obligations.
